repository_purpose: Unified MCP server for multi-provider model prompting and CEO-and-board style arbitration across LLM vendors.

runtime: provider SDK/API access or local Ollama

findings: This is a useful escalation or challenge lane, not a parent core primitive.
The `ceo_and_board` pattern is the strongest parent-relevant feature because it creates a governed arbitration step when peer consensus is insufficient.
Provider prefixes and output-file paths make the repo suitable for traceable review artifacts if the parent ever promotes a challenger lane.

capability_rows.validation_method: Validate that escalation prompts record board-member outputs, CEO decision output, provider provenance, and explicit reasons for any final override.
capability_rows.blocker_or_dependency: Requires a running just-prompt MCP server plus provider credentials or a local-model equivalent; without those, the lane remains gated and must not be treated as default.

trigger_logic: Invoke only when a peer-mesh or validator lane needs an explicit challenge, arbitration, or board-style decision.
Do not promote just-prompt into the default parent path because peer mesh and hook policy remain the first-line control surfaces.
actor_logic: The production gatekeeper or challenge arbiter owns invocation and evidence review.
validation_summary: Require saved decision artifacts and provider provenance.
Reject hidden escalation that leaves no machine-readable board or CEO outputs.

overlaps: Can complement peer mesh when flat peers reach an explicit escalation point.
Shares model-provider boundaries with pi-vs-claude-code `.env` usage but is not required for mesh operation.
blockers: Gated on credentials or local-model configuration for the chosen providers.

source_refs.note: Documents the MCP tools, provider prefixes, parallel prompting, and CEO-and-board workflow.
Pins the Python MCP server runtime for later implementation work.

github_verification.note: GitHub due diligence pinned the cited upstream files to the verified commit snapshot used for this packet.
